data.name: Press Secretary for the Mayor of Busan
data.role: Press Secretary for the Mayor of Busan
data.informationNeed: I am the press secretary to Park Heong-joon, the mayor of Busan. I am the person chiefly responsible for all of the mayor's media appearances, for directing the office's communications strategy, and for delivering press briefings about important events in and around the city to outlets such as Yonhap, JoongAng Ilbo, Busan Ilbo, and KBS/MBC regional bureaus. I also coordinate heavily with my counterparts in central government in Seoul when Busan municipal policy and national policy intersect. I am fluent in both English and Korean.

data.name: Structures Specialist with the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board
data.role: Structures Specialist with the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board
data.informationNeed: I am an employee of the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board. I assist with, and occasionally lead, investigations into aeronautical accidents. My background is as a structures specialist, meaning that I assess and report on damage to the body of aircraft involved in the accidents: I analyze airframe damage, breakup patterns, and whether structural failure was a cause or consequence of the accident. When working in this capacity (i.e. not as the lead of an investigation), I do not generally concern myself with casualties or with investigations into whether crew and air traffic control procedures were correctly followed.

data.name: In-House Counsel for Nitto Denko
data.role: In-House Counsel for Nitto Denko
data.informationNeed: As in-house counsel for Nitto Denko, I advise the company's global operations on legal matters across its three core business segments—Optoelectronics & Imaging, Life & Healthcare, and Industrial Tape & Specialty Products—ensuring compliance with the complex regulatory frameworks of the various jurisdictions where the company operates. I manage contract negotiations with major electronics manufacturers, medical device distributors, and industrial customers worldwide, and also support M&A deals. Another major part of my role involves intellectual property protection, given Nitto Denko's heavy investment in R&D and its extensive patent portfolio in areas like optical films, adhesive technologies, and membrane filtration. I also work closely with leadership to navigate cross-border compliance issues—including trade regulations, environmental standards, and data privacy laws—across Nitto Denko's operations in Japan, the United States, Europe, and Southeast Asia.

data.name: Director of the Daegu Fire Department
data.role: Director of the Daegu Fire Department
data.informationNeed: I oversee all fire suppression, emergency medical response, and rescue operations across Daegu's eight districts, ensuring rapid and effective response to the city's roughly 2.5 million residents. I manage the department's budget, personnel, and training programs in coordination with the National Fire Agency, which sets national standards and policy frameworks that guide local operations. I work closely with Daegu's city government and neighboring regional fire authorities to maintain mutual aid agreements and disaster preparedness plans, particularly given the city's industrial areas and periodic risk of large-scale emergencies. Additionally, I lead public fire prevention initiatives and ensure our stations and equipment meet the standards required by Korean fire safety law.

data.name: Administrator of the Korean Heritage Service
data.role: Administrator of the Korean Heritage Service
data.informationNeed: I serve as the vice minister-level head of South Korea's central government agency responsible for preserving, managing, and promoting the nation's cultural, natural, and intangible heritage. I oversee the designation and direct management of State-designated Cultural Heritage—including National Treasures—while also supporting local governments in their stewardship of City- and Province-designated properties, and my approval is required for any alteration to protected heritage sites or excavation of underground and underwater cultural properties. I am responsible for submitting Korea's World Heritage, Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, and Memory of the World candidates to UNESCO, and for strengthening international cooperation in the heritage field through partnerships with other nations. Under my leadership, the Korea Heritage Service directly manages the royal palaces and tombs of the Joseon Dynasty—including Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung Palaces—and oversees institutions such as the National Palace Museum of Korea, the National Research Institute of Maritime Cultural Heritage, and the Korea National University of Cultural Heritage.

data.name: POSCO Public Relations Representative
data.role: POSCO Public Relations Representative
data.informationNeed: I protect and promote POSCO's global reputation. I work to communicate the company's achievements and values to media, investors, governments, and the general public. A growing part of my work involves highlighting POSCO's sustainability commitments, particularly its pledge to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 and its development of HyREX, a proprietary hydrogen reduction ironmaking technology Posco-inc. I also manage messaging around POSCO's expanding business portfolio, helping stakeholders understand the company's evolution beyond steel into areas like battery materials, including anode and cathode materials for rechargeable batteries and investments in lithium production.

data.name: Analyst at the National Typhoon Center (Korean Meteorological Administration)
data.role: Analyst at the National Typhoon Center (Korean Meteorological Administration)
data.informationNeed: I monitor and analyze the development, movement, and intensity of tropical cyclones across the western Pacific and surrounding regions, drawing on satellite imagery, numerical model outputs, and observational data to produce timely and accurate typhoon forecasts. When a storm threatens the Korean Peninsula, I work closely with colleagues in the KMA's Forecast Bureau to issue track and intensity guidance, storm surge outlooks, and public warnings that feed into national disaster preparedness decisions. My work requires close coordination with international partners—including the Japan Meteorological Agency and the Joint Typhoon Warning Center—to reconcile competing model forecasts and build consensus on a storm's likely behavior. Based at our center in Seogwipo on Jeju Island, I am often on the front lines of typhoon season from July through October, operating under significant time pressure when a rapidly intensifying storm is bearing down on the peninsula.

data.name: Research Associate, Civic Engagement and Social Movements at The Asia Foundation
data.role: Research Associate, Civic Engagement and Social Movements at The Asia Foundation
data.informationNeed: I am a Research Associate with the Civic Engagement and Social Movements team at The Asia Foundation’s Korea Office, where I conduct qualitative research on protest activity, public participation, and civic discourse across the region. My work involves collecting and analyzing primary sources such as social media content, government statements, and local and international news coverage, then synthesizing that material to identify themes, narratives, and patterns in mobilization and state response. I maintain structured databases of civic events, track shifts in public messaging across platforms, and prepare annotated briefs and background memos to support senior researchers and program staff. I also contribute to regional reports on civil society trends by translating raw information into clear, evidence-based summaries.

data.name: Policy & Member Support Officer, Korea Auto Industries Coop. Association (KAICA)
data.role: Policy & Member Support Officer, Korea Auto Industries Coop. Association (KAICA)
data.informationNeed: I support small and mid-size automotive components manufacturers who are members of KAICA by monitoring market and regulatory changes that could affect their business, including shifts in vehicle technology requirements, new OEM entrants, and evolving procurement practices. My work involves preparing briefing materials, policy position papers, and market intelligence reports to help member companies anticipate structural changes in the Korean automotive supply chain—particularly the shift toward EV and hydrogen powertrains, which require different components than traditional ICE vehicles. I also coordinate KAICA's participation in government consultations and industry events, representing our members' interests on issues such as EV component localization standards and supplier transition support programs. My goal is to ensure Korea's component supplier ecosystem remains competitive as domestic and international automakers accelerate their electrification strategies.

data.name: Fire Investigation Officer (화재조사관), Gyeonggi-do Fire & Disaster Headquarters
data.role: Fire Investigation Officer (화재조사관), Gyeonggi-do Fire & Disaster Headquarters
data.informationNeed: I am a certified fire investigation officer (화재>조사관) attached to the Gyeonggi-do Fire & Disaster Headquarters, where I specialize in determining the origin, cause, and pattern of spread of fires at commercial and industrial sites throughout Gyeonggi Province. My work involves conducting systematic post-fire scene examinations, collecting and preserving physical evidence, interviewing facility personnel and witnesses, and producing official investigation reports used by prosecutors, insurers, and occupational safety regulators. I hold the certified fire investigator credential managed by the National Fire Agency (소방청), which requires ongoing professional development and periodic examination to maintain. My goal is to produce accurate, legally defensible findings that support accountability for fire losses and contribute to fire prevention policy in Gyeonggi's industrial areas.

data.name: North Korean Military Affairs Analyst, Overseas Operations Division, National Intelligence Service (NIS / 국정원)
data.role: North Korean Military Affairs Analyst, Overseas Operations Division, National Intelligence Service (NIS / 국정원)
data.informationNeed: I work in the National Intelligence Service's division responsible for monitoring North Korean military activities, including the overseas deployments and covert operations of DPRK armed forces and the foreign policy decisions that drive them. My responsibilities include maintaining current assessments of DPRK army unit capabilities, leadership structures, and operational postures, drawing on a range of collection disciplines and close liaison relationships with allied intelligence services in the US, Japan, and partner states. I track North Korean military personnel movements and training activities and produce finished intelligence assessments for senior government and military consumers, including the Ministry of National Defense, the Blue House National Security Office, and the Joint Chiefs of Staff. My goal is to provide early warning of changes in North Korean military behavior that could affect the security of the Republic of Korea or its allies, and to support allied partners with timely Korean-language expertise when DPRK personnel or materials are encountered outside the peninsula.

data.name: Senior Secretary (선임비서관, Grade 5), Democratic Party of Korea Lawmaker's Office, National Assembly
data.role: Senior Secretary (선임비서관, Grade 5), Democratic Party of Korea Lawmaker's Office, National Assembly
data.informationNeed: I work as a senior secretary (선임비서관, Grade 5) for a Democratic Party of Korea lawmaker in the National Assembly, responsible for coordinating my principal's legislative schedule, drafting floor statements and press remarks, managing constituent relations, and maintaining working relationships with party leadership and committee staff. As one of up to nine personal staff a lawmaker may employ under the National Assembly Act, I am embedded in the daily rhythms of the legislative process—tracking bills through committee, coordinating with the National Assembly Secretariat (국회사무처) on procedural matters, and ensuring my lawmaker is briefed and positioned ahead of floor votes and public hearings. My office is in the National Assembly complex in Yeouido, and I spend most working hours—and many non-working hours—on the grounds. With the Democratic Party holding 175 seats in the current Assembly, making it the largest bloc, the pressure on our team to advance the party's legislative agenda against a minority presidential government has been unrelenting.

data.name: Events Program Manager, Han River Business Headquarters (한강사업본부), Seoul Metropolitan Government
data.role: Events Program Manager, Han River Business Headquarters (한강사업본부), Seoul Metropolitan Government
data.informationNeed: I am an events program manager within the Han River Business Headquarters (한강사업본부), the Seoul Metropolitan Government division responsible for managing operations across Seoul's eleven Hangang riverside parks. My role involves planning, coordinating, and overseeing large public events held at Hangang Park facilities—including cultural performances, seasonal festivals, and special outdoor shows—from initial concept through post-event review. I coordinate across multiple city departments and external vendors to secure venue permits, manage crowd safety logistics, and ensure that all events meet the Seoul Metropolitan Government's standards for public engagement, accessibility, and safety. My goal is to maximize Hangang Park's value as a vibrant civic and cultural space for Seoul residents and international visitors alike, while managing the operational complexity of running events in one of the city's most densely visited public spaces.

data.name: Senior Investigator, Corruption Investigation Office for High-ranking Officials (CIO / Gongsocho)
data.role: Senior Investigator, Corruption Investigation Office for High-ranking Officials (CIO / Gongsocho)
data.informationNeed: I am a senior investigator at the CIO, the only agency in South Korea with the authority to investigate and indict high-ranking public officials — including the President, ministers, judges, and senior military officers — without interference from the regular prosecutor's office. My day-to-day work involves building complex criminal cases against individuals who often have deep institutional resources, legal teams, and political allies working to obstruct or delay proceedings. I manage warrant applications, coordinate with the courts, oversee evidence collection, and make judgment calls about when and how to execute arrests in environments that may be legally ambiguous or physically resistant.

data.name: Research Fellow, Korea Democracy Foundation (민주화운동기념사업회), Seoul
data.role: Research Fellow, Korea Democracy Foundation (민주화운동기념사업회), Seoul
data.informationNeed: I study the health and resilience of South Korea's democratic institutions, with a particular focus on how constitutional mechanisms perform under stress. My research tracks how the National Assembly exercises its oversight powers, how citizens mobilize in response to perceived abuses of executive authority, and how Korea's hard-won democratic norms — forged through decades of pro-democracy struggle — hold up against contemporary political crises. I produce policy briefs and long-form reports that are read by legislators, civil society groups, and international democracy monitors. Much of my work involves comparing Korea's institutional responses to political crises with those of peer democracies in East Asia and beyond, asking what structural features make some systems more resilient than others and where Korea's framework still has gaps that reformers should address.

data.name: Gangdong-gu District Office Road Facilities Management Team Leader
data.role: Gangdong-gu District Office Road Facilities Management Team Leader
data.informationNeed: I lead the Road Facilities Management Team at Gangdong-gu District Office, where I am responsible for overseeing the maintenance, inspection, and repair of road surfaces and underground utility corridors across our district's 24 administrative dong neighborhoods. My team coordinates with contractors to ensure scheduled road inspections are completed on time and that damage reports submitted by residents are properly logged, prioritized, and addressed. I liaise regularly with the Seoul Metropolitan Government's Urban Infrastructure Headquarters to align district-level maintenance programs with citywide underground safety initiatives. My primary goal is to maintain safe road conditions and identify potential ground subsidence risks before they escalate into public safety hazards.

data.name: Color Commentator, Worlds English Broadcast (Contracted by Riot Games)
data.role: Color Commentator, Worlds English Broadcast (Contracted by Riot Games)
data.informationNeed: I am a color commentator and on-air analyst for the League of Legends international esports broadcast, contracted by Riot Games to cover major competitive events throughout the year. My job is to provide real-time strategic analysis during live matches, explaining draft decisions, in-game macro plays, and teamfighting tactics in a way that is engaging for both casual viewers and seasoned competitive fans. I work closely with play-by-play casters and the production team to ensure that my analysis is accurate, timely, and calibrated to the broadcast's pacing and editorial tone. Between matches I participate in desk segments where I offer breakdowns of team strategies alongside other broadcast talent, drawing on my own background as a former semi-professional player to lend credibility and depth to my commentary.

data.name: Program Officer, Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA), Republic of Korea
data.role: Program Officer, Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA), Republic of Korea
data.informationNeed: I am a Program Officer at the Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA), the central South Korean government agency responsible for planning, budgeting, and managing defense procurement programs for the Republic of Korea Armed Forces. My primary responsibilities include evaluating domestic and foreign defense technology proposals against acquisition program requirements, coordinating with the Agency for Defense Development (ADD) and Defense Agency for Technology and Quality (DTaQ) on capability assessments, and preparing procurement recommendation reports for DAPA's senior leadership and the Defense Project Promotion Committee. I track developments in unmanned systems, AI-enabled platforms, and manned-unmanned teaming technologies as part of a broader effort to modernize the Korean military's force structure within our current mid-term defense acquisition plan. My role sits at the intersection of technical evaluation and interagency coordination, requiring close engagement with both the Korean defense industry and foreign original equipment manufacturers.
